title: Polymer clay sculpted bear figurine
subtitle: A small seated bear modelled from two colours of polymer clay
excerpt: A seated teddy-bear-style figurine sculpted in brown and cream polymer clay. The body, head, limbs, and facial features are modelled separately and assembled before curing. No kiln is required: the piece hardens in a domestic oven at 130°C. The finished figurine stands about 6 cm tall.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Polymer clay sculpture methods are a widely documented craft technique.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling material that hardens in a domestic oven at 110 to 130°C; not a true ceramic
An internal wire or foil support structure around which clay is built up, used in larger sculptural pieces to add strength without bulk

content.text: Polymer clay sculpture at small scale needs no
armature
because the pieces are short and solid. The bear below is built in sections and assembled before curing so all parts fuse together in the oven into a single piece.
Polymer clay
holds fine detail at this scale, making ear cups, eye indentations, and paw pads easy to model with a needle tool. No kiln is required.

materials.name: Polymer clay, cream or pale beige (for muzzle and ear cups)
Small black glass beads or black polymer clay (for eyes)

tools.name: Wooden rib or ball stylus for eye indents

content.text: Conditioning
Condition both colours by rolling and folding each one until it is smooth and pliable. Keep the cream separate from the brown until ready to use.
Body parts
Body: roll 20 g of brown clay into an oval roughly 4 cm long and 3 cm wide. Flatten the base slightly so the bear can sit upright.
Head: roll 10 g of brown clay into a ball about 2.5 cm in diameter. Slightly elongate the lower front of the ball to suggest a snout area.
Ears: roll two small brown balls about 8 mm in diameter. Press each flat with a thumb. Press a small disc of cream clay into the centre of each ear cup.
Limbs: roll four short sausage shapes of brown clay for arms and legs, each about 2 cm long and 8 mm thick. Flatten one end of each leg slightly for the paw.
Muzzle: roll a small oval of cream clay about 1.5 cm wide and 1 cm tall. Press it flat against the front of the head.
Assembly and detailing
Press the head onto the top of the body. Blend the neck join by smoothing clay from the body up onto the back of the head with a finger.
Press the ears onto the top sides of the head. Blend each ear base into the head with the needle tool.
Press the arms against the upper sides of the body and the legs at the lower front, angled so the bear appears seated. Blend each join.
Press two small black beads into the head above the muzzle for eyes. Use a needle tool point to press a small nostril into the muzzle and a curved line below for the mouth.
Add three short lines to each paw front with a needle tool to suggest claws.
Curing

Place the figurine on a ceramic tile and cure in a domestic oven at 130°C for 30 minutes. Support the bear upright with a small folded card prop if needed. Ventilate the kitchen during curing. Do not use the curing oven for food cookware.
Use and care
Decorative only. Not food-safe. Not suitable for dishwasher, microwave, or contact with solvents. Wipe clean with a dry cloth.
Variations
Make a family of three in different sizes at 40 g, 60 g, and 80 g of clay.
After curing, paint the bear with watered-down acrylic washes to add shading depth to the fur texture scored with a needle tool.
Troubleshooter

items.problem: Head detaches from body after curing
items.cause: The join was not blended enough before curing and the two pieces did not fuse
items.fix: Reattach with a small amount of liquid polymer clay or cyanoacrylate adhesive and cure again at 130°C for 15 minutes

items.cause: The base was not flat enough for the bear to sit upright on its own
items.fix: Prop upright with a folded card support during curing. After curing the base can be sanded flat

items.cause: The beads were not pressed deep enough into the soft clay before curing
items.fix: Press replacement beads into small divots drilled with the needle tool and secure with cyanoacrylate adhesive
